The list can grow mid-session (an MCP server finishes connecting, or the user connects a third-party connector). If a tool you need is not listed yet, re-check on later turns rather than assuming it cannot exist; just do not guess names or invent namespaces that never appear here.

This list carries only the connectors the user has already connected, and the organization may offer more that are simply not connected yet. An app missing from this list therefore never means no connector exists for it: do not tell the user the app is unavailable, and do not fall back to a browser, scraping, a shell command, or a generic skill, before you have checked what the organization offers.

If that app is offered, call `tools.ConnectApp` inside a Script with app="<slug>" to produce a connect link for the user and ask them to connect. Fall back to another route only after ConnectApp shows the app is not offered.
ConnectApp connects a connector, not an MCP server; after connection, use only the connector tools that appear in this list.

The logs/ folder holds 300 CI job logs. A job's result is the LAST line in its file that starts with
"STATUS:". Earlier STATUS lines are from retries and do not count. Write report.json in the repository
root with exactly this shape: {"failed_count": <int>, "failed_jobs": [<job ids, sorted ascending>]}.
A job id is the file name without ".log". Do not change the logs.

Performance tip: call `tools.TodoWrite` in the same Script as your next tool calls to save user's time and tokens.</system-reminder>

I wrote `report.json` to the working directory. This folder isn't a git repository, so I treated the working directory as the repository root. 55 of the 300 jobs failed.

```json
{"failed_count": 55, "failed_jobs": ["job-002", "job-006", ..., "job-291"]}
```

For each job, I took the last line in its log that starts with `STATUS:` and counted the job as failed if that line was `STATUS: FAILED`. The logs contain 491 `STATUS:` lines in total, because retries add extra ones. Every log has at least one, and each one reads either `STATUS: PASSED` or `STATUS: FAILED`, so no job was left unclassified.

The job ids in the file are sorted ascending, and I didn't change the logs.
